Settings redesign

Four layouts of the member Settings pages, regrouped and renamed. Prototype on branch prototype/settings-redesign, fake member data with the real country and service lists, nothing saves. Screenshots at 1440 px and 390 px.

Not ratings, release dates, interface language or SEO.

The language and region finding

“Country” is about availability and age ratings. “Titles” is the language of title names, posters and descriptions. They are independent, but the tab groups them as one pair, and the country is split from the services it decides.

  • Country sets where to watch, service badges, Discover's streaming filters, Newly available, which services the Streaming tab offers, and the age ratings. It changes no language.
  • “Titles” reads like a filter on which titles appear. It only changes title names, posters, descriptions and taglines. Menus, genres and the title analysis stay English.
  • Your services are saved per country on a different tab, so a country change can leave “my services” empty without saying so.
  • Three country stores still exist: the saved pair, the old country_default row, and a guest localStorage country that some views prefer.
  • Possible bug, outside this prototype: saving the pair doesn't refresh the cached user-settings and streaming-providers queries, so “your services” can show the old country for up to a minute.

Proposed grouping

GroupHoldsWhy
Where you watchYour country (was “Country”), Your services (was the Streaming tab)Services depend on the country. Today a country change can quietly empty “my services” on another tab.
Title languageTitle language (was “Titles”), with a live previewIts own group, so it no longer reads as part of the country.
Public profileHandleUnchanged.
Your dataImports, Hidden titlesBoth are about your library, not about preferences.
Connected appsApps and the connector addressUnchanged, still hidden while Better Auth is off.
Account and sign-inSign-in methods with the email shown, Password, Restart setup (was “Restart Onboarding”), Delete account (placeholder)Everything about the login in one place.

All four variants use these groups and names. They differ only in layout.

Naming: country and language

Questions for you

  1. Country: keep Your country with the line “Streaming offers and age ratings”, or use Streaming country (shorter, but hides the age ratings), Watching from, or Region?
  2. Language: is Title language clear, or do you prefer Language of titles and descriptions or Show titles in?
  3. Should country and services share one group (Where you watch), with the title language on its own, as proposed? Today country and language share a tab.
  4. The language picker says menus stay in English. Is that the promise you want on this page, or should it stay quiet about the interface?

The variants

A One page

Every setting on one scrolling page in six groups, with a sticky index: a sidebar on a desktop, a row of chips on a phone.

  • Nothing hides behind a tab, so nobody hunts for a setting.
  • Country and services sit side by side, then the title language with a live preview.
  • Long page. Deep links become anchors (/settings#where).

Route: /prototype/settings/a

B Summary list

A grouped list of rows. Each row shows what is set now: the flag and country, your service logos, the title language. A row opens its editor beside the list on a desktop, or in place of the list on a phone.

  • You see every current value at a glance, without opening anything.
  • Familiar from phone settings apps.
  • One more tap on a phone to change something.

Route: /prototype/settings/b

C Grouped tabs

Today's sidebar of tabs, regrouped under three headings (Watching, Your data, Account) and renamed. One topic per tab. On a phone the tabs become a scrolling row.

  • The smallest change from today, and the cheapest to build.
  • Existing links (/settings/streaming, /settings/imports, /settings/connected-apps) keep a home.
  • Still one page per topic, so the overview problem stays partly.

Route: /prototype/settings/c

D Tiles (bolder)

A profile header, then big tiles that show each setting's effect instead of its name: the flag with your service logos, a poster with its title in your title language. A tile opens its editor in a sheet, from the right on a desktop and from the bottom on a phone.

  • The most visual: the language tile shows what the setting does.
  • Profile and account move to the header, where people look for them.
  • Bigger departure from today. Sheets animate with transform and opacity only.

Route: /prototype/settings/d

Questions for you

  1. Which variant: A One page, B Summary list, C Grouped tabs, or D Tiles? Or a mix, such as D's language preview tile inside B's list.
  2. Change email and Delete account don't exist yet. The variants show Delete account as a placeholder. Build them as part of the redesign, later, or not at all?
  3. Restart setup (today “Restart Onboarding”): keep it under Account and sign-in, or move it under Where you watch?
  4. Two settings live outside Settings: the Discover “For you” toggle and cookie consent. Bring either into Settings?
